_comment: TECH-102: reaping on what the CONTAINER says, not on a clock. Every claim
here is FRESH - one minute old against the harness's --now - so the 45-minute
timeout cannot fire for any of them. Anything released here is released
because /status said the worker had stopped, and for no other reason.
#70  exited 6      -> released immediately (the case that cost 45 minutes)
#71  running       -> survives. THE POSITIVE CONTROL, inverted: without it,
a reaper that released everything would pass #70.
#72  gone, old     -> released: no container, and the claim outlived the
#73  gone, seconds -> survives: the claim comment is written BEFORE the
container exists, so a reaper racing a dispatcher
must not take the ticket off a worker being born
#74  exited 0 with an open PR -> survives. The file lock is held until a
human MERGES, not until the worker finishes.
#75  exited, unknown to /status -> falls back to the clock, and its claim
is fresh, so it survives. Not knowing is not dying.
Liveness comes from the sidecar the harness writes next to the record file
(<record>.status.json), which is what RecordingSpawner answers /status from.
Nothing here is real: the repo, the paths and the commands are invented.

issues.title: Worker exited 6 thirty seconds ago
body_lines: Its acceptance command failed and the container stopped.

issues.title: Worker is running right now
body_lines: Working. Reaping this destroys work in progress.

issues.title: No container, and the claim is older than the spawn grace period
body_lines: Its container vanished - OOM-killed, or removed by hand.

issues.title: No container yet, claimed seconds ago
body_lines: Claimed, container not created yet. The race the grace period exists for.

issues.title: Worker exited 0 and its pull request is open
body_lines: Finished. Its files stay reserved until a human merges.

issues.title: Liveness cannot be determined
body_lines: The spawn dispatcher could not be asked. Not knowing is not dying.
